summary: This article explains why more than half of your body is water, the jobs water does inside you, how you lose it, and how to drink enough, especially in a hot Saudi summer.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Water and Your Body” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: not having enough water in your body
the parts of food that your body needs to grow and stay healthy
to change from a liquid into a gas and go into the air

challengeTerms.def: to move around through a system and come back to the start
to control something and keep it at the right level
to clean something by passing it through a part that catches what is not wanted

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that you only need to drink water when you feel thirsty? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Imagine you are planning a school sports day in June. Using facts from the article, explain what you would do to keep everyone from becoming dehydrated.
struggling: Pre-teach dehydrated, nutrients, and evaporate with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses circulate, regulate, and filter to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
